# New renderings, iliad-140 (22.188–288)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἀσπερχὲς κλονέων (22.188) | "unceasingly throwing into confusion" | "without pause, throwing him into confusion" | "relentlessly", "harrying", "driving in rout"; follows the table's ἀσπερχές "unceasingly" / "without pause" and κλονέω "throw into confusion" |
| ἄγκεα · βήσσας (22.190) | "valleys" · "glens" | "valleys" · "glens" | "dales", "ravines", "thickets"; ἄγκος and βῆσσα are told apart as open valley and wooded glen |
| ποδώκεα Πηλεΐωνα (22.193) | "the fleet-footed son of Peleus" | "the fleet-footed son of Peleus" | "swift of foot" (πόδας ὠκύς); follows the table's ποδώκης Πηλεΐων (8.474) |
| οὐ λῆθε (22.193; λανθάνω with the accusative) | "did not escape the notice of" | "did not escape the notice of" | "was not hidden from", "did not elude"; the same wording at 22.277 λάθε … Ἕκτορα "escaped the notice of Hector" |
| ἀλάλκοιεν βελέεσσι (22.196; no object in the Greek) | "might keep harm off him with missiles" | "might keep harm off him with their missiles" | "ward off" (reserved for ἀμύνω), "defend him"; "harm" is supplied and the note says so; follows the table's ἀλάλκοι "keep … away" |
| ἀποστρέψασκε (22.197; iterative -σκ-) | "he would turn back" | "would turn him back" | "turned back" (loses the repetition) |
| ἐν ὀνείρῳ (22.199) | "in a dream" | "in a dream" | "in a nightmare", "in sleep" (ἐνύπνιον) |
| ἤντετ’ ἐγγύθεν (22.203–204) | "had met, near at hand" | "had met him … close at hand" | "come to his aid", "stood by him"; ἀντάω "meet" |
| ἐπῶρσε μένος λαιψηρά τε γοῦνα (22.204) | "roused might and quick knees" | "roused might and swift knees in him" | "strength" (reserved for κράτος / σθένος), "fury"; follows the table's μένος "might" and λαιψηρά "quick" (10.358) |
| λαοῖσιν δ’ ἀνένευε καρήατι (22.205) | "signed a refusal with his head" | "made a sign of refusal with his head" | "shook his head" (the Greek says the head is thrown back); follows the table's ἀνανεύω "signed a refusal" / "made a sign of refusal" (21.129) |
| πικρὰ βέλεμνα (22.206) | "bitter missiles" | "bitter missiles" | "sharp", "cruel"; follows the table's πικρὸν ὀϊστόν "bitter arrow" (4.118) |
| κῦδος ἄροιτο βαλών · ὃ δὲ δεύτερος ἔλθοι (22.207) | "win the glory by striking him, and he come second" | "win the glory by striking him, and he himself come second" | "take the credit", "arrive second"; κῦδος "glory" |
| ἐπὶ κρουνοὺς ἀφίκοντο (22.208) | "came to the springs" | "reached the springs" | "fountains", "streams"; follows the table's κρουνώ "the two springs" (22.147) |
| τὸ τέταρτον (22.208) | "for the fourth time" | "for the fourth time" | "the fourth time round", "on the fourth lap" (add "round"/"lap" the Greek does not have) |
| χρύσεια … τάλαντα (22.209, a repeated line) | the published wording ("golden scales") | the published wording ("his golden scales") | none; the line is carried over word for word from the published unit (it ends in a comma here, not ·) |
| ἐν δ’ ἐτίθει δύο κῆρε τανηλεγέος θανάτοιο (22.210) | "and in them he placed two death-spirits of death that lays-at-length," | "and in them he put two spirits of death that lays men at length," | the published wording, carried into a new unit; the second line (22.211) is new: τὴν μὲν Ἀχιλλῆος, τὴν δ’ Ἕκτορος ἱπποδάμοιο "the one of Achilles, the other of Hector, horse-taming" / "one for Achilles and one for Hector, tamer of horses" (the table's ἱπποδάμοιο, 7.404) |
| ἕλκε δὲ μέσσα λαβών (22.212) | "and he drew it, having taken it by the middle" | "and he took it by the middle and drew it up" | "lifted", "weighed", "held up the scales" (each decides the picture); ἕλκω "draw, pull" |
| ῥέπε δ’ Ἕκτορος αἴσιμον ἦμαρ (22.212) | "and sank Hector's fated day" | "and Hector's fated day sank" | "day of doom", "the day of fate"; follows the table's ῥέπε δ’ αἴσιμον ἦμαρ Ἀχαιῶν (8.72) |
| ᾤχετο δ’ εἰς Ἀΐδαο (22.213; δόμον understood) | "and went off to the house of Hades" | "and went off to the house of Hades" | "into Hades' realm", "down to Hades" (loses the genitive); the note says "house" is understood |
| λίπεν δέ ἑ Φοῖβος Ἀπόλλων (22.213) | "and left him Phoebus Apollo" | "and Phoebus Apollo left him" | "forsook", "abandoned"; Φοῖβος Ἀπόλλων is the table's "Phoebus Apollo" |
| Πηλεΐωνα δ’ ἵκανε θεὰ γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη (22.214) | "To the son of Peleus came the goddess, gleaming-eyed Athena," | "The goddess, gleaming-eyed Athena, came to the son of Peleus," | "grey-eyed", "bright-eyed", "owl-eyed"; γλαυκῶπις keeps "gleaming-eyed" as in the table's θεὰ γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη (1.206) |
| νῶι … ἔολπα … οἴσεσθαι μέγα κῦδος Ἀχαιοῖσι προτὶ νῆας (22.216–217) | "I expect, we two, … to bear off great glory for the Achaeans to the ships" | "I expect, we two, … shall carry off great glory for the Achaeans to the ships" | "hope" (kept for ἔλπομαι of a good outcome in the table's 1.545, and weaker here), "win"; ἔολπα "I expect" (cf. ἔλπομαι "expect", 9.40); νῶι dual "we two" |
| Διῒ φίλε φαίδιμ’ Ἀχιλλεῦ (22.216) | "dear to Zeus, glorious Achilles" | "glorious Achilles, dear to Zeus" | "beloved of Zeus", "shining Achilles"; follows the table's Διῒ φίλε (11.611) and φαίδιμος "glorious" (4.505) |
| μάχης ἄατόν περ ἐόντα (22.218; ἄατος "insatiable", sense not certain) | "insatiable of battle though he is" | "insatiable of battle though he is" (+ note: usual sense, not certain) | "unwearied of fighting", "never tired of war" (each fixes the sense), "unapproachable" |
| οὔ οἱ … ἔστι πεφυγμένον ἄμμε γενέσθαι (22.219) | "it is no longer possible to have escaped us" | "he can no longer escape us" | "there is no escape for him from us" (loses the perfect) |
| ἑκάεργος Ἀπόλλων (22.220) | "far-working Apollo" | "far-working Apollo" | "far-shooting" (ἑκηβόλος), "far-darting" (ἑκατηβελέτης); the table's ἑκάεργος (1.479) unchanged, with its note that the meaning is disputed |
| προπροκυλινδόμενος πατρὸς Διὸς αἰγιόχοιο (22.221) | "rolling himself forward before father Zeus, aegis-bearing" | "rolling himself over and over before his father, aegis-bearing Zeus" | "grovelling", "prostrating himself" (each decides the posture); follows the table's αἰγιόχοιο Διός "aegis-bearing Zeus" (5.733) |
| ἄμπνυε (22.222) | "get your breath" | "get your breath" | "rest", "recover", "take heart"; ἀναπνέω "breathe again" |
| ἐναντίβιον μαχέσασθαι (22.223) | "to fight face to face" | "to fight you face to face" | "to fight hand to hand", "to meet him in battle" |
| ὣς φάτ’ Ἀθηναίη, ὃ δ’ ἐπείθετο, χαῖρε δὲ θυμῷ (22.224) | "So spoke Athena, and he obeyed, and rejoiced in his heart," | "So Athena spoke, and he obeyed and was glad at heart," | "was delighted", "his spirit was glad", "he was persuaded"; ἐπείθετο "obeyed" (middle of πείθω), χαίρω θυμῷ "rejoice in heart" |
| μελίης χαλκογλώχινος (22.225; χαλκός "bronze" + γλωχίς "point") | "bronze-pointed ash-spear" | "bronze-pointed ash-spear" | "bronze-tipped", "bronze-barbed", "bronze-headed"; μελίη "ash-spear" (2.543) |
| Δηϊφόβῳ ἐϊκυῖα δέμας καὶ ἀτειρέα φωνήν (22.227) | "like Deiphobus in body and in unwearied voice" | "taking the likeness of Deiphobus in body and in his unwearied voice" | "in form and untiring voice", "in build and tireless voice"; follows the table's δέμας καὶ ἀτειρέα φωνήν (13.45) |
| ἠθεῖ’ (22.229, 22.239; vocative; sense not known) | "my honoured one" | "my honoured one" (+ note: sense not known) | "dear brother", "old friend"; follows the table's ἠθεῖε / ἠθεῖος (10.37, 14.147) |
| βιάζεται (22.229) | "presses hard" | "is pressing you hard" | "overpowers", "harasses", "forces"; βιάζομαι "use force on" |
| ποσὶν ταχέεσσι (22.230) | "on swift feet" | "on swift feet" | "fleet-footed", "swift-footed"; "swift" for ταχύς (13.436) |
| γνωτῶν οὓς Ἑκάβη ἠδὲ Πρίαμος τέκε παῖδας (22.234) | "of the kinsfolk, the children whom Hecuba and Priam bore" | "of all my kin, the children whom Hecuba and Priam bore" | "brothers" (the table's γνωτός avoids it, though here it means siblings), "kinsmen"; follows γνωτούς "kinsfolk" (3.174) |
| νοέω φρεσὶ τιμήσασθαι (22.235) | "I intend in my mind to honour" | "I am minded to honour you in my heart" | "I think of honouring", "I resolve"; νοέω "intend, have in mind" |
| ὑποτρομέουσιν (22.241) | "tremble beneath" (τοῖον … "for such a one they all tremble beneath") | "they all tremble so before him" | "shudder", "are terrified"; τοῖον left open between "such a one" and "so", as the note says |
| πένθεϊ λυγρῷ (22.242) | "grievous grief" | "grievous grief" | "bitter grief", "wretched sorrow"; follows the table's λυγρός "grievous" (3.416, 5.156) and πένθος "grief" (4.197) |
| μὴ δέ τι δούρων ἔστω φειδωλή (22.243–244) | "let there be no sparing of spears" | "let there be no sparing of spears" | "no holding back", "let us spare no spear"; φειδωλή "sparing" |
| ἔναρα βροτόεντα · νῆας ἔπι γλαφυράς (22.245–246) | "bloody spoils" · "to the hollow ships" | the same | the table's ἔναρα βροτόεντα (8.534) and νῆας γλαφυράς (10.531), unchanged |
| ὣς φαμένη καὶ κερδοσύνῃ ἡγήσατ’ Ἀθήνη (22.247; κέρδος "gain") | "So saying, and with cunning, led the way Athena;" | "So speaking, Athena led them on with her cunning;" | "craftily", "with guile", "shrewdly"; κερδοσύνη "cunning" (a word of gain-seeking skill) |
| οὔ σ’ ἔτι … φοβήσομαι (22.250) | "Not any more you … shall I fear" | "I shall no longer be afraid of you" | "I shall no longer flee from you", "I fear you no more" in both layers; φοβέομαι "fear" |

| ἔκπαγλον ἀεικιῶ (22.256) | "treat terribly unseemly" | "abuse terribly" | "mutilate", "outrage"; follows the table's ἀεικίσσωσι "treat unseemly" / "abuse" (16.545) and ἐκπάγλως "terribly" |
| καμμονίην (22.257; sense not certain) | "staying-power" | "endurance" (+ note: exact sense not certain) | "victory", "the upper hand", "strength to hold out" (each decides the unknown) |

| λέουσι καὶ ἀνδράσιν ὅρκια πιστά · λύκοι τε καὶ ἄρνες (22.262–263) | "faithful oaths for lions and men" · "wolves and lambs" | "faithful oaths between lions and men" · "wolves and lambs" | "trustworthy oaths", "binding oaths"; the table's ὅρκια πιστά "faithful oaths" (2.124) |

| ὣς οὐκ ἔστ’ ἐμὲ καὶ σὲ φιλήμεναι (22.265) | "it is not possible for me and you to be friends" | "there can be no friendship between you and me" | "to love one another", "to be at peace"; φιλέω "be friends" |
| πρίν γ’ ἢ ἕτερόν γε πεσόντα αἵματος ἆσαι Ἄρηα ταλαύρινον πολεμιστήν (22.266–267) | "before at least one, having fallen, has glutted with blood Ares, the shield-enduring warrior" | "until one or the other has fallen and glutted Ares, the warrior who bears the hide shield, with his blood" | the published wording for the last line (029, from 5.289), unchanged; "before" for πρίν γ’ ἢ in `l` and "until" in `i` |

| ἠλεύατο (22.274) · ἄλευαι (22.285) | "avoided" · "avoid" | "avoided" · "avoid" | "dodged", "evaded", "shunned" (kept for ἀλυσκάζω "shunning"); ἀλέομαι "avoid" in both places |
| ἕζετο γὰρ προϊδών (22.275) | "for he sat down, seeing it beforehand" | "for he crouched, having seen it beforehand" | "ducked", "stooped", "bent low" (each decides the picture); ἕζομαι "sit down" in `l` |

| ἐν γαίῃ δ’ ἐπάγη (22.276) | "and in the earth it stuck" | "and stuck in the earth" | "was fixed", "was lodged" (the table's ἠρήρειστο "was driven"); ἐπάγη "stuck, was fixed" |

| mark values (22.216, 229, 233, 239, 250, 261, 279) | — | "Athena speaks", "Athena speaks, as Deiphobus", "Hector answers", "Athena answers", "Hector speaks", "Achilles answers", "Hector speaks" | — |

Whole-line formulas carried over word for word from published units, with no change: ἀγχοῦ δ’ ἱσταμένη ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα (22.215, 22.228); ἀλλ’ ἄγε δὴ στέωμεν καὶ ἀλεξώμεσθα μένοντες (22.231); τὴν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπε μέγας κορυθαίολος Ἕκτωρ (22.232); τὸν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπε θεὰ γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη (22.238); τὸν δ’ ἄρ’ ὑπόδρα ἰδὼν προσέφη πόδας ὠκὺς Ἀχιλλεύς (22.260). Partly carried over: 22.209, 22.210 (first line), 22.248 (first line), 22.267, 22.269 (second line), 22.273 (first line).
